html:
A battle fought in July 552 in the Apennines of central Italy, where the eastern Roman army of Narses defeated the Ostrogoths under their king Totila. It decided the Gothic War.

Totila had won back most of Italy in the 540s. Justinian gave Narses a large army, including many Lombard and other allied warriors. Narses set his allies on foot in the centre and massed archers on the wings. When the Gothic cavalry charged the centre, the archers shot them down from both sides, and the Gothic army broke. Totila was badly wounded in the flight and died soon after.

The Goths chose a new king, Teia, who was killed near Vesuvius a few months later. The battle effectively ended the Ostrogothic kingdom. Procopius gives the main account.
